summary: Adds three HTTP endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter guarded by a mutex, and an upstream status probe. main.go registers all three routes.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search copies the name query parameter straight into the SQL text with Sprintf. Any quote in the name ends the string literal and lets the caller add SQL.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can read or change any data the database user can reach.
findings.fix: Use a placeholder in the query and pass name to QueryContext as a bound argument.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex stays locked when key is missing
findings.problem: Count takes h.mu and then returns early when key is empty. That path never releases h.mu.
findings.consequence: A single request to GET /count with no key blocks every later Count request forever. Those requests pile up as stuck goroutines.
findings.fix: Check key before taking the lock, or release the lock with defer right after Lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before the error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil.
findings.consequence: Every request to GET /upstream panics while the upstream is unreachable, so the caller never gets the 502 response.
findings.fix: Move the deferred Close below the error check.

findings.title: New handlers have no tests
findings.problem: No test covers the new Search, Count and Upstream handlers. The repository has no Go test files at all.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches bugs like the stuck lock or the nil response panic before they ship.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each handler, including the missing key and unreachable upstream paths.

dropped.reason: This hit flags the same Sprintf query as c1. The c1 finding already covers it.
